title: Prefer clear English to Latin abbreviations
text: Prefer familiar English phrases to Latin abbreviations in editable controlled prose. Use for example to introduce illustrations and that is to introduce a restatement or definition. Preserve the distinction between a non-exhaustive example list, an exact restatement, and an open-ended set. Omit an unnecessary abbreviation only if no meaning or scope is lost. Do not use etc. or and so on in place of a complete list of required actions, prerequisites, or permitted values. State such a list completely, or provide an authoritative reference that defines the complete set and its applicable version.
exceptions: An example list is not an exhaustive specification, and a restatement must not broaden or narrow its subject. If the intended scope is unclear, obtain clarification rather than choose an expansion from the abbreviation alone.

Preserve quotations, authoritative names, interface strings, identifiers, and other externally or machine-controlled text exactly in marked literal spans. Explain an unfamiliar abbreviation outside the preserved span instead of silently changing it.
Do not remove necessary qualifications, conditions, or safety and security context to simplify wording. Escalate conflicting external requirements to the responsible editor or technical owner.
Examples judge this rule only and do not approve a vocabulary. Supporting target IDs are planning references, not canonical relation endpoints or delegated source allocations.

segments.text: Illustrative list: The report can include diagnostic details, for example, request times and response codes. Exact local value set: The only permitted modes are manual and automatic.

allowed.rationale: For example marks illustrations without asserting completeness; the separate permitted-value sentence explicitly states its complete local set.

segments.text: The legacy help text contains the abbreviation
. In this quoted text it means for example, not that is.

allowed.rationale: The exact quoted abbreviation remains unchanged, and surrounding English explains its illustrative function without converting it into a definition.

segments.text: Editorial context: the local mode set contains only manual and automatic. Specification: Permitted modes are manual, automatic, and so on.

not_allowed.rationale: An open-ended ending contradicts the complete value set and leaves validation requirements undefined. Expanding etc. to and so on would not solve the scope problem.

segments.text: Editorial context: request times and response codes are two examples among several possible diagnostic details. Rewrite: Diagnostic details, that is, request times and response codes, appear in the report.

not_allowed.rationale: That is presents the two examples as an exact restatement and narrows the category. Retain for example when the intent is illustration.

facets.source_facet: Latin abbreviations can be unfamiliar, so English expansions help readers understand the intended relationship.
facets.rationale: Prefer clear English in IT prose while preserving exact external text and distinguishing examples from restatements; see docs/it-ste-research/W2-editorial-review.md.

facets.source_facet: The source illustrates abbreviations for examples, clarification, and continuation of a list.
facets.rationale: Preserve those distinct functions and require complete operational or value specifications rather than merely expand an open-ended abbreviation; see docs/it-ste-research/W2-editorial-review.md.

criteria: Review ASD-STE100 Issue 9 guidance GR-6 on physical PDF page 126; preserve guidance kind and distinguish the source's clarity recommendation from the added IT completeness requirement.
Check whether each list illustrates, defines, or enumerates a complete set. Verify any authoritative reference and its version; never infer omitted required values or actions.

Review original wording, examples, quotation digest, exceptions, applicability, separate ASD rights, attribution, and planned dependencies. Automated checks do not establish list completeness, vocabulary approval, or legal rights.
